text:
Dallas hosts Montreal tonight with the Stars trying to bounce back from a 5-1 loss to New Jersey that ended their five-game winning streak. The Canadiens have won three straight, the latest a 2-0 shutout in St. Louis where Florian Xhekaj scored his first NHL goal. They are doing it without Nick Suzuki and Ivan Demidov. Oliver Kapanen has moved in beside Slafkovský and Caufield, and Chris Kreider has taken Demidov's spot.

Our numbers see little between the teams at five on five, where MTL has 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and DAL 54%. Dallas has the cleaner recent run, with 57% of the expected goals over its last five against Montreal's 50%, and our model puts tonight at 3.21 to 2.68 for the Stars. Dallas also has the better special teams, and Montreal's 5.2 penalties a game keep handing opponents power plays. In net, Jake Oettinger (projected) is at +9.3 goals saved above expected this season, while Jakub Dobes (projected) is at -5.8, though he finished last season at +17.3 over 43 games.

For Dallas, Wyatt Johnston (40% to score) and Jason Robertson (38%) lead our list, and Mikko Rantanen is the likeliest to record two or more points at 35%. For Montreal, Cole Caufield, who wears an "A" tonight in Suzuki's absence, as The Hockey News' Karine Hains posted, is our pick at 32% to score. Alexandre Texier is one goal from 50 career goals.
